bullets: CRL 2026 series decider (video t=2454-2614, broadcast footage with no readable clock). Ryley and his coach picked this list specifically to beat log bait: "me and my coach actually chose this deck, assuming that he could go for a log bait deck" (t=2464-2468), "here we went for a deck with arrows just to have a good chance. We even had mother witch, valky, ghost. We just really needed as many bait counters as possible in this matchup" (t=2488-2496). It is his Bandit/Freeze bridge-spam list with Royal Ghost and Arrows in those two slots, Valkyrie played as the Heroic Valkyrie.

The bridge cards are aimed at cards, not towers: Royal Ghost at [2, 17] to kill the Dart Goblin (t=2498.5), Mother Witch onto the Skeleton Army for Cursed Hogs (t=2504-2508), Arrows at [6, 26] behind it "just to try to get an early lead" (t=2514.5).

Elite Barbarians are the deck's tempo card in this matchup rather than a damage threat: bridge E-Barbs at [14, 18] (t=2570.6) "because I wanted to mess up his cycle", and they trade off the Dark Prince (t=2574-2584); he explicitly rates them "not really that great in this match" against Skarmy plus Dark Prince (t=2588).

Defence is Valkyrie or Battle Ram plus a 1-elixir Heal Spirit: Valkyrie at [4, 18] he expects to lose plus Heal Spirit at [8, 18] holds the whole left side for zero damage (t=2528-2540). The one failure is a mis-placed Battle Ram kite at [8, 13] (t=2564.2) that costs roughly half his right tower (3052 -> 1613 HP).

The win-back is a full bridge-spam stack: Mother Witch and Zappies from the back (t=2588.6, t=2590.6), then Valkyrie at [13, 18], Evo Battle Ram at [15, 17], Heal Spirit and Arrows plus the Wild Whirlwind ability at the tower (t=2598-2608) — "I took out the entire tower in one push" (t=2612). The clip ends mid-sentence, so the game result is not shown.

Own-deck caveat: the perception pipeline filed every deploy at or past the river as an opponent play and read four extra cards off a 0.49-confidence hand reader; this eight-card list is rebuilt from the deploy labels plus Ryley's commentary. See the match file's Data gaps.

new_deck.rationale: Battle Ram, Royal Ghost and Elite Barbarians are dropped at the bridge for tempo and card trades, with Mother Witch, Valkyrie and Zappies as the defensive core — the standard bridge-spam shape.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: A bait-counter build of Ryley's bridge-spam list: Royal Ghost and Arrows take the Bandit and Freeze slots so that every one of Skeleton Army, Princess, Dart Goblin and Goblin Barrel has a cheap answer, while Mother Witch turns an enemy swarm into Cursed Hogs instead of just clearing it. The bridge cards are used to force specific cards out of hand — Royal Ghost to make the opponent spend a Dark Prince, Elite Barbarians to break their cycle — and the damage arrives afterwards as an Evolution Battle Ram plus Heroic Valkyrie (Wild Whirlwind) push supported by Zappies, Heal Spirit and Arrows. The weakness Ryley shows in the same game is placement risk: the deck defends with kites, and one mis-clicked Battle Ram kite cost him half a tower.
